title: A VICTORY REMEMBERED, A FAILURE NOTED

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: that is, the whole kingdom of Og in Bashan, who had reigned in Ashtaroth and Edrei. (He was the last of the Rephaites.) Moses had defeated them and taken over their land. But the Israelites did not drive out the people of Geshur and Maakah, so they continue to live among the Israelites to this day - Josh 13:12-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two things sit side by side in these verses, and we should not miss either. First, a victory: the defeat of Og, the last of the giant Rephaites, a triumph God gave through Moses. Second, a failure: Israel did not drive out the people of Geshur and Maakah, and so they remained "to this day."

Scripture is honest. It records the triumphs and the shortfalls with equal candour. Israel had won great victories, but there was disobedience too — ground left unclaimed, a task left half done. The Bible does not airbrush God's people into heroes. It tells the truth, and in doing so it tells the truth about us as well.

That unclaimed ground would have consequences. What Israel tolerated would later become a snare. This is a sober lesson: the compromises we make peace with, the areas we decide are "not worth the fight," rarely stay contained. They tend to linger and trouble us later. Yet the honesty of Scripture is also a mercy. It shows us our need for a Saviour who never left a single task undone. Where Israel — and we — fall short, Christ finished the work completely (John 17:4), and His grace covers even our unclaimed ground.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What compromise have you made peace with that God calls you to confront?
- Are you honest with yourself about both your victories and your failures?
- How does Christ's completed obedience give you hope where you fall short?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I confess the areas where I have made peace with what You call me to confront. Thank You that Christ finished the work I cannot, and that His grace covers my failures. Amen.
